extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers and journalists interested in AI-generated political misinformation and propaganda
extracted.subtask_description: A concise encyclopedic definition and characterization of 'slopaganda' — AI-generated content intended to manipulate political beliefs, emotions, or decision-making — distinguishing it from traditional propaganda and from low‑quality AI content more generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core definition — AI-generated content designed to manipulate beliefs, emotions, and political decision-making at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Slopaganda is a portmanteau of "AI slop" and "propaganda", referring to AI-generated content designed to manipulate beliefs, emotions, and political decision-making at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term credited to Michał Klincewicz (2025). Serves as the article's primary definitional criterion for identifying instances of slopaganda: content must be AI-generated and be intended to manipulate political cognition or decisions at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing features: scale, scope, and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Slopaganda is distinguished from traditional propaganda by three features: scale, scope, and speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative AI enables production of large volumes of content quickly and at low cost (scale); allows highly personalised and targeted messaging to specific sub-audiences (scope); and leverages the hyper-connectivity of social networks to accelerate dissemination beyond what conventional media could achieve (speed). These three dimensions are the primary axes for evaluating whether material qualifies as slopaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-targeting / personalization (vs uniform messaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike traditional propaganda, which delivers a uniform message to all recipients, slopaganda can be micro-targeted — tailored to individuals based on estimated prior beliefs to reinforce political biases or emotional associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether messaging is tailored to specific sub-audiences or individuals using inferred priors. Micro-targeting that aims to reinforce existing biases or emotional associations is characteristic of slopaganda and helps differentiate it from one-size-fits-all propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive rather than truth-apt (not necessarily deceptive)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors note that it need not aim at literal deception: much slopaganda is expressive rather than truth-apt, designed to create emotional associations rather than false factual beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should not rely solely on factual falsehoods; content that focuses on evoking emotions or associations (even if not strictly false) can be slopaganda. Look for manipulative affective framing, symbolic or associative content, and emotional appeals intended to shape political attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent-based distinction from AI slop
rubrics_metrics.description: Slopaganda is a subset of AI slop — low-quality, mass-produced AI-generated content — distinguished by intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While AI slop may be produced for commercial reasons or engagement-farming, slopaganda is specifically deployed with a deliberate political or ideological goal. Determinations should consider the producer's apparent intent and the political/ideological targeting of the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production characteristics: low-quality, mass-produced, rapid, low-cost generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Slopaganda leverages generative AI to produce large volumes of content quickly and at low cost; it is often low-quality and mass-produced (AI slop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess production traits such as repetitive/formulaic output, low fidelity, and the use of automated pipelines. These production features enable scale and frequency that amplify political manipulation when combined with targeting and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactics and illustrative forms (deepfakes, mixed footage, themed videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable examples discussed include Iranian Lego-themed videos depicting political figures; AI-generated videos mixing real military footage with clips from films and video games; and deepfake audio imitating political candidates during the 2024 US presidential campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying slopaganda, consider use of deepfakes, synthetic audio, manipulated video (including mixes of real and fabricated footage), and themed or meme-style content as common tactics. Examples demonstrate how various media manipulations serve the defining criteria (intent, scale, targeting, emotional effect).
